headline: GOLD RECLAIMS $4,050 AS POST-FED RELIEF TRADE TAKES HOLD — Metal Climbs From 3-Month Low Despite 80%+ December Hike Odds
snippet: Spot gold recovered above $4,050 on October 30 after the Federal Reserve's October 28 hold decision triggered a modest relief trade, with Whalesbook citing a 0.77% gain to $4,056 in the immediate aftermath. The bounce comes off the $3,994 three-month low reached mid-week as December rate-hike odds remain elevated above 80% — the underlying headwind for gold has not cleared, but near-term technicals show oversold readings across the gold complex that have historically preceded tactical bounces.

headline: IMC RARE EARTHS HITS 2,052 ppm YTTRIUM OVER 7m IN BRAZIL — Block H Zone Opens Heavy Rare Earth Upside at Itarantim, Next Steps ANSTO Leach Tests
snippet: IMC Rare Earths (NYSE MKT: IMCR) disclosed two high-grade yttrium discoveries at its Itarantim ionic adsorption clay project in Bahia, Brazil: Block H returned 7 metres at 2,052 ppm YO3 (peak 3m at 2,836 ppm), and Block D returned 13 metres at 1,287 ppm YO3, both starting within 2 metres of surface. Multiple samples exceeded the lab's 500 ppm upper measurement limit. Yttrium has end-use applications in aerospace, semiconductors, and advanced ceramics. Next steps include infill and step-out drilling and independent leach testwork at ANSTO in Australia.

headline: UR-ENERGY LAUNCHES 120-HOLE LOST CREEK SOUTH CAMPAIGN — Three Rigs to Test 16-Square-Mile Wyoming Uranium Property Adjacent to Producing Mine
snippet: Ur-Energy (TSX: URE / NYSE: URG) announced a 120-hole exploration program at its Lost Creek South property in Wyoming, targeting an under-explored 16-square-mile block immediately adjacent to its operating Lost Creek ISR mine. Three drill rigs are mobilised for Q3–Q4 2026 work. With uranium long-term contract prices still above $95/lb, the company is aggressively expanding its resource base ahead of potential multi-mine production scenarios at the Lost Creek processing hub.

headline: ANFIELD ENERGY WINS DRAFT STATE PERMITS FOR SHOOTARING URANIUM MILL — Utah Facility Targets Final License Q2 2027 for Historic ISL Restart
snippet: Anfield Energy received a draft renewed operating license and draft groundwater discharge permit from Utah state regulators for its Shootaring Canyon uranium mill — a processing facility originally built in the 1980s that has sat idle for decades. A final renewed license is targeted for Q2 2027, after which Anfield would be one of only a handful of licensed uranium mills operating in the United States. The milestone is a meaningful de-risking event for a company building toward production in an undersupplied domestic market.

headline: ICONIC MINERALS WRAPS PHASE 1 AT NEW PASS, NEVADA — Near-Surface Gold-Silver Final Assays In From Churchill County Exploration
snippet: Iconic Minerals (TSXV: ICM) completed Phase 1 drilling at its New Pass gold and silver property in Churchill County, Nevada, with all assays now received from the final three exploration holes. The program tested near-surface targets at a property the company characterises as a large-footprint, multi-element system. Results will inform whether a Phase 2 expansion program proceeds; Nevada's Churchill County basin has seen a cluster of junior discoveries in the 2024–2026 exploration cycle.

headline: TERRA CLEAN ENERGY FINISHES DRILL PADS AT MARYSVALE UTAH URANIUM SITE — Mobilization Revised to Late November; Historic Mine Area Targeted
snippet: Terra Clean Energy completed drill pad construction and trenching at its Marysvale Uranium Mines Project in Utah, advancing site preparation ahead of the first drill holes at a historic uranium-vanadium district. Equipment availability pushed the mobilization timeline from early November to late November 2026. The Marysvale District produced uranium ore for decades through the 1980s, and Terra is among a wave of junior companies revisiting known historical uranium districts in the Mountain West as long-term contract prices hold above $95/lb.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER PREMIUM SURGES TO 13-YEAR HIGH — Chinese Physical Demand Holds Near-Record $14,360/t Despite LME Inventory Build
snippet: The Yangshan copper import premium — a real-time gauge of Chinese physical demand — surged to $205 per tonne, its highest level in over 13 years, even as LME inventories ticked higher and three-month copper eased to around $14,363 per tonne. The divergence is significant: a rising Yangshan premium alongside a rising inventory figure suggests strong underlying Chinese demand that is absorbing new arrivals rather than signalling oversupply. World Bank lifted its copper price outlook 18% earlier this month.

headline: USA RARE EARTH +13%, CRITICAL METALS +12% AS SECTOR BID BROADENS — REMX ETF Gains 4% in Critical Minerals Stock Surge
snippet: Critical minerals stocks surged in a broad sector rally on October 27, with USA Rare Earth (USAR) jumping 13%, Critical Metals rising 12%, TMC up 11%, United States Antimony gaining 11%, and MP Materials advancing 7%. The VanEck rare earth ETF (REMX) gained 4% on the day. Analysts tied the move to renewed speculation around US government critical mineral supply-chain policy following Rio Tinto's $1.4B Argentina lithium openings and Australia's commitment to the Donald rare earths project — sector catalysts that signal a global investment wave in non-Chinese critical mineral supply.

headline: GOLD'S WORST 'MAY BE OVER' — Analyst Says 25% Pullback Has Fully Priced December Rate-Hike Risk
snippet: A mining analyst argues that gold's 25% retracement from its January 2026 all-time high above $5,300 has fully discounted even the most hawkish Federal Reserve scenarios, citing RSI readings in the 28–33 range across the gold complex — historically extreme oversold territory. The piece frames December as the make-or-break moment: if the Fed hikes and gold holds $3,900, the bull market correction is likely complete; if it fails $3,900 on a hike, a deeper reset toward $3,600 would need to be absorbed before resuming the structural uptrend.

headline: COPPER, URANIUM, LITHIUM SELLOFF PUTS TECHNICAL SUPPORT AT RISK — Multi-Commodity Outlook Flags Key Levels to Watch Heading Into Q4
snippet: FX Empire's latest multi-commodity technical analysis identifies critical support levels across copper ($13,800/t LME), uranium spot ($90/lb) and lithium carbonate (CNY 85,000/t) that are at risk of being tested in Q4 2026 amid a general pullback in industrial commodities. Copper's near-record Yangshan premium provides bullish fundamental support, while lithium continues to bleed after the CNY 90,000 floor break; uranium's tight long-term contract market is seen as insulating spot from the broader selloff. Junior miners exposed to all three metals face heightened share-price volatility through year-end.
